name: City Council Meeting
minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Agency,
  Community Development Financing Authority,
  Public Improvement Corporation,
  and Library Board of Trustees*

  November 1, 2010

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Agency, the Community
Development Financing Authority, the Public Improvement Corporation, and the Library Board
of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Kelley at 5:04
p.m., on November 1, 2010, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on October 27, 2010, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Ledesma
  Council Member Schlicht (arrived at 5:05 p.m.)
  Council Member Ury
  Mayor Pro Tem Leckness (arrived at 5:19 p.m.)
  Mayor Kelley

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Irwin B. Bornstein, Assistant City Manager/Director of Admin. Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Schlicht

INVOCATION: Council Member Ledesma

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Ariel Valli, Ladera Ranch: asked for an update on the Oso/Marguerite intersection improvement
project.

City Council Minutes  1  November 1, 2010
 City Manager Wilberg announced that the work is progressing ahead of schedule and the project
is expected to be completed in the summer of 2011.

CLOSED SESSION

CS1.  Conference with City Attorney Concerning One matter of Existing Litigation Pursuant to
  Government Code Section 54956.9(a). The Litigation is City of Mission Viejo v.
  Saddleback Valley Unified School District (SVUSD), Case No. 00300610.

RECESS AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:08 p.m., Mayor Kelley declared a recess to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:01 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council was given an update on the litigation but
there was no reportable action.

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Presentation by Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) in Recognition of
  Community Service by the OCFA Reserve Firefighters

  Mayor Kelley and Fire Chief Rick Robinson presented certificates of appreciation to the
  Mission Viejo Reserve Firefighters.

P2.  Proclaim November 6, 2010, as Scouting for Food Day

  Mayor Kelley presented the proclamation to Bill Grennell, Boy Scouts Saddleback
  District Executive from Troop 1215, Marie and Gabrielle Whitcomb from Brownie Troop
  348, and Theodora Haniotis from Girl Scout Troop 900.

P3.  Proclaim the Month of November as Pulmonary Hypertension (PH) Month

  Mayor Kelley presented the proclamation to Shashi Sahgal, Betty Lou Wojciehowski,
  group leader and past group leader of the Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension Support
  Group at Mission Hospital.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Mazi Bahadori, M.V.: expressed concern with Mayor Kelley’s statements after City Council
candidate Rick Sandzimier was allegedly struck by a car while out placing election signs.

Steven Guess, M.V.: noted that Council candidate Sandzimier is employed by Parsons

City Council Minutes  2  November 1, 2010
 Brinkerhoff and he recommended that the city’s contract with PB be terminated if candidate
Sandzimier is elected to the City Council.

Joyce Saltzgiver, M.V.: stated that the Murray Community and Senior Center is the brightest
jewel in the city’s crown and she thanked the Council for the facility. Mrs. Saltzgiver also
reminded residents to vote in tomorrow’s election.

Dan Avery, M.V.: announced that he and his wife Victoria are founding sponsors of "Toys for
Watts" which will be held this year on December 11, 2010. He invited anyone with a motorcycle
to participate in the toy drive and to visit his web site (www.theinsufferabledanavery.com) for
more information.

Bill Monohan, M.V.: on behalf of the Marine Adoption Committee, he announced that Disney
has introduced a military promotion to provide a large discount on Disneyland tickets for
military personnel and their families.

Neil Lonsinger, M.V.: discussed his qualifications for City Council Member and he asked
residents for their vote in tomorrow’s election.

Ken Golemo, M.V.: stated that the election season has been tense and stressful but he is glad that
he participated in the process of running for a seat on the City Council.

Susan Sellers, M.V.: expressed appreciation for the many amenities available to residents of
Mission Viejo and encouraged residents to vote for Trish Kelley, Dave Leckness and Rick
Sandzimier in the election tomorrow.

Rick Sandzimier, M.V.: stated that he trusts that voters will show their wisdom and validate his
comments in tomorrow’s election.

Elaine Portnoy, M.V.: commended the Council for establishing Mission Viejo as a City of
Character.

Diane Mill, M.V.: expressed concern with activity surrounding political signs and encouraged
residents to research the candidates well before voting.

Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: read a statement from resident Brian Goodell, co-chair of the Citizens
to Protect Mission Viejo, who found a political advertisement in the Saddleback Valley News
that was credited to their committee when in fact, the committee did not authorize or pay for the
ad.

Robert Reidel, M.V.: thanked the City Council for unanimously voting to oppose Measure H and
he encouraged residents to vote no on Measure H in tomorrow’s election.

Dennis O’Connor, M.V.: expressed concern with activity surrounding the election and the

City Council Minutes  3  November 1, 2010
 actions of a small group of people who are attempting to gain control of the City Council. He
encouraged residents to vote for Trish Kelley, Dave Leckness and Rick Sandzimier.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 3 and 4 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said
  titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title
  and further reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of October 18, 2010, as
  presented.

5.  Biennial City Commission Member Term Expiration

  (1) Directed the City Clerk to post the Notice of City Commission Vacancies, (2) set
  application deadline for December 17, 2010, and (3) scheduled appointment of
  commission members for January 3, 2011.

6.  Notice of Completion-CDBG-R 2009 Residential Asphalt Overlays (CIP 838)

  (1) Certified the completion of and accepted the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City
  Clerk to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the
  faithful performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days, respectively, after the
  date of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being
  filed with the City; and (4) authorized payment of the final retention 35 days after the
  date of recordation of the Notice of Completion.

7.  Notice of Completion-Los Alisos Boulevard Overhead Methacrylate Deck

City Council Minutes  4  November 1, 2010
   Treatment (CIP 836)

  (1) Certified the completion of and accepted the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City
  Clerk to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the
  faithful performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days, respectively, after the
  date of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being
  filed with the City; and (4) authorized payment of the final retention 35 days after the
  date of recordation of the Notice of Completion.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

OLD BUSINESS

NEW BUSINESS

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

3.  Check Register dated October 8, 2010, in the amount of $1,146,958.33

  Council Member Schlicht noted that there were three expenditures on the check register
  for Turf Lane Park and she asked when she will be getting a final list of payments for the
  park rehabilitation project.

  City Manager Wilberg responded that he will be distributing an update to the City
  Council Members this evening.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, ratify the
  accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

4.  Check Register dated October 15, 2010, in the amount of $465,738.21

  Council Member Schlicht asked about the legal bills associated with her name on page 13
  of the check register.

  City Attorney Bill Curley announced that it related to the litigation and he will follow up
  and provide the Council with details.

City Council Minutes  5  November 1, 2010
   Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to ratify
  the accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS

8.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Mayor Kelley announced that there has not been a recent meeting of the OCFA Board of
  Directors.

9.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Kelley presented the report.

10.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Kelley presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

City Manager Wilberg announced that he has provided the City Council Members with a
cumulative update of the costs associated with the Turf Lane Park rehabilitation.

City Attorney's Report

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

11.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as
  presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Ledesma

Council Member Ledesma stated that the highlight of the last two weeks was the Walk Against

City Council Minutes  6  November 1, 2010
 Drugs and he thanked staff and the Orange County Sheriff’s Department, as well as participants
from the two different school districts.

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht announced that the Mission Viejo Diablos won another football game
last weekend and she enjoyed being there to cheer them on. She encouraged residents to read the
City Council Candidate statements, trust and verify the information, and vote their conscience.
She stated that she looks forward to the upcoming Veteran's Day ceremony as a way to celebrate
and honor our country's veterans.

Council Member Ury

Council Member Ury stated that the Walk Against Drugs was a wonderful event and he was very
impressed by the young speaker, Sarah Lonsert. He also discussed his attendance at the Home
Town Halloween celebration and he thanked staff and the Saddleback Recreation Department for
an outstanding job. Council Member Ury reminded residents to get out and vote tomorrow and
to exercise their intelligence at the polls. He observed that there are a lot of things that are
positive about the city and it is sometimes difficult for people to say thanks for everything that
they have become used to. He stated that he believes there are several City Council candidates
who are dedicated to making sure that residents will continue to receive the things that they
enjoy about Mission Viejo.

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness outlined his attendance at the Walk Against Drugs and stated that one
of the highlights was the Sheriff's Department demonstration of a bomb diffusing robot. He also
discussed his attendance at the Hometown Halloween celebration and expressed his appreciation
for the opportunity to sit at the front desk at the Community Center and greet the residents as
they arrived. Mayor Pro Tem Leckness shared a story about his chance meeting with a resident
who picks up trash on his morning walks. The resident conveyed an idea to make t-shirts with
the slogan “Walking around Mission Viejo With a Bag Attitude” and how he’d like to implement
a program to encourage other residents to pick up trash on their daily walks. Mayor Pro Tem
Leckness thanked Council Member Ledesma for doing a great job while he served on the City
Council and he stated that it has been a privilege to sit next to John Paul for the last eight
months.

Mayor Kelley

Mayor Kelley concurred with Mayor Pro Tem Leckness’ statements and expressed her own
appreciation to Council Member Ledesma. She also commended the Police Services
Department, Crime Prevention Specialist Tammy Descoteaux, the different groups that
participated and planned this year’s Walk Against Drugs, and Supervisor Pat Bates who provided
the Disaster Preparedness element. She believes that the Walk Against Drugs is the most
important thing we do as a city and this year was especially poignant for her because, following

City Council Minutes  7  November 1, 2010
 the event, she attended a funeral for a young Mission Viejo man who was caught in the trap of
addiction and who died. She encouraged parents to talk to their children, stay informed, and
seek help if they need it. Mayor Kelley congratulated the Capistrano Valley High School
Foundation on their very successful Taste of Capo event. It was a great fundraiser and all the
money that was raised will go back to Capistrano Valley High School. She also reminded
residents to mark their calendars for the city’s Veterans Day ceremony on November 11, 2010, at
2:00 p.m. at the Murray Community Center. She noted that there is another ceremony at El Toro
Memorial Park at 11:00 a.m. that day. Mayor Kelley encouraged residents to vote in tomorrow’s
election and if they are still unsure about the candidates, they can view the Candidate Forum
through Cox Cable On Demand. Finally, she announced that the Community of Character word
for the month of November is thankfulness.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 7:35 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Kelley adjourned the meeting to Monday, November 15, 2010, at 5:00 p.m.

__________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of November 15, 2010

City Council Minutes  8  November 1, 2010
